questions.q: What is the key difference between a list and a tuple?
options: A tuple can hold more items than a list
A list can only hold numbers; a tuple can hold any type
There is no real difference between them
A list is mutable (can be changed after creation); a tuple is immutable
questions.explain: Lists can be modified after creation; tuples cannot.

questions.q: Given customer_ids = [501, 502, 501, 503], what does len(set(customer_ids)) return?
options: 3, because a set keeps only unique values
0, sets cannot be measured with len()
4, same as the list
1, because sets collapse everything into one value
questions.explain: A set removes duplicates, so {501, 502, 501, 503} becomes {501, 502, 503}, which has 3 elements.

questions.q: What does line_totals[-1] return for line_totals = [259.98, 249.50, 79.00]?
options: An error, because -1 is not a valid index
259.98, the first item
The number of items in the list
79.00, the last item in the list
questions.explain: Negative indexing counts from the end, so -1 refers to the last item.

questions.q: Why might a function return a tuple instead of a list?
options: Tuples run computations faster than any other data type
Functions are not allowed to return lists
Tuples can only contain strings
A tuple signals a fixed, complete result, such as multiple return values from a function
questions.explain: Returning multiple values as a tuple is a common, idiomatic Python pattern, covered further in Lesson 9.

questions.q: What does "West" in regions_we_ship_to check, if regions_we_ship_to is a set?
options: How many times 'West' appears in the set
Whether the set is empty
Whether 'West' is alphabetically first in the set
Whether the string 'West' is a member of the set
questions.explain: The 'in' operator performs a fast membership check on a set.
